places.name: The City of Light
places.description: A vast inhabited city seen either from a distance (glowing on the horizon, across a valley, beyond a doorway of cloud) or entered and walked through. People describe wide avenues, towers and buildings so tall they vanish into cloud, and a light that comes from the material of the city itself rather than from any sun. Several say it is 'made of light' though it looks like gold, crystal or white stone. Many arrive at it after the tunnel or after meeting a guide, and it is usually the largest single made thing they see.

aliases.note: the most common phrasing; frequently paired with 'city of God' by the same speaker
used by Dannion Brinkley and repeated by many later experiencers
explicitly tied to Revelation 21 by biblically-framed narrators
plural form used by Monroe-influenced narrators; more than one city
rare non-ornate variant: featureless box-like buildings, no windows or doors

places.regex: \bcit(y|ies) of (light|gold|god)\b|golden cit(y|ies)|crystal(line)? cit(y|ies)|shining city|celestial city|holy city|cit(y|ies) of heaven|heavenly city|new jerusalem
places.negative_regex: velocity|new york city|kansas city|salt lake city|mexico city|city council|inner city|city of santee

quotes.text: I saw this other realm that was like a, a city of light.
a crystal city, celestial city, magnificent place. There, I, I could see wide avenues, and also buildings that were so tall
And beyond it was this beautiful crystal city. I'll never forget it with the waterfalls on the side.
And I saw this golden city way in the distance.

I was in some sort of city with flat ground; there were buildings with no windows nor doors, just like big boxes.

places.notes: Strongly enriched among the best-evidenced accounts: 2.56% of all docs but 6.08% at cv>=23 - roughly 2.4x. Most speakers see the city rather than enter it; the commonest verb is 'saw ... in the distance'. A minority explicitly reject it ('I thought heaven was streets of gold and pearly gates - it wasn't like that'), which the regex still catches; those are counted as false positives in the precision estimate above only when the speaker never saw a city at all.

places.name: The Buildings
places.description: Constructed edifices in the otherworld, described generically before the speaker knows what any of them is for. People repeatedly say they 'noticed a building' and then somehow knew, without signage or being told, what it was: a university, a library, a nursery, a place of healing. Buildings are often walked through rather than into - one experiencer says each building he entered opened into a different realm. Several note that the buildings shape-shift or reconfigure themselves to the needs of whoever is inside.

aliases.note: by far the commonest word
where souls prepare for a lifetime

places.negative_regex: hospital building|apartment building|office building|school building on|building up|pressure was building|building a case|the building was on fire|out of the building|in the building where

quotes.text: there were buildings there. I remember going through the buildings, the different buildings.
I could see that it was this huge vast building. It was built out of one piece of marble
I remember seeing sort of buildings, is what I could describe them in human terms, in the background.
In these buildings, I saw stairs leading from floor to floor, but there was no elevator. I saw roads, but there were no cars.
And then I noticed this building. And I had so many questions about the building.
I woke up inside of a beautiful building.

places.notes: The clearest cvNDE gradient in this region: 11.32% overall rising monotonically to 21.55% at cv>=23. Precision losses are almost entirely earthly buildings seen during the out-of-body phase (hospital, apartment block, city skyline seen while floating), which is itself an interesting confound because those OBE sightings are what earn the high cvNDE scores.

places.name: What the Buildings Are Made Of
places.description: A recurring, unusually concrete detail: the material of the built world. Marble, crystal, glass, pure gold, and - most distinctively - 'living stone', a white quartz-like substance with swirling markings that people insist is alive and conscious. Several say the buildings are hewn from blocks of light rather than stone, which is why they have warmth. Furniture inside is the same stuff: marble tables, marble benches, crystal tablets, a glass door with glass hinge pins that could not stand up under earthly physics.

aliases.note: white quartz-like, with visibly moving markings; described as alive and praising God
used where a speaker compares the building to the Parthenon but insists it is not stone

places.regex: (made|built) (of|out of) (marble|crystal|living stone|pure gold)|buildings? (made|built|hewn) (of|out of|from) light|(marble|alabaster|crystal|living stone|white stone) (floor|floors|building|buildings|steps|walls|columns|pillars|tables)

these columns, beautiful, tall white marble, maybe 30 feet high
Everything was made of a very clear glowing crystal.
it appeared that all the buildings, they appeared to be as if they were made of gold

places.notes: Rare (1.23%) and flat across strata, with a single cv>=23 hit, so treat the stratum comparison as noise. Included because it is the single most concrete and most cross-culturally repeated physical claim in the built region: the material of heaven is alive.

places.name: The Great White Building with Columns
places.description: A specific, repeatedly described edifice: an enormous glowing white or pearlescent building fronted by tall columns, approached up a long flight of stairs, with a huge doorway at the top. Spirit-beings in white robes are milling around outside, going in and coming out. Speakers who have no vocabulary for it reach for 'Greek or Roman temple'. Inside, it usually opens into the library or hall of records - the columns and the books belong to the same structure.

aliases.term: like a Greek or Roman temple
aliases.note: the single most common comparison; the speakers stress they are only borrowing the shape

aliases.term: the Parthenon, but hewn from blocks of light

sensory: columns roughly 20-30 feet high, about six feet apart, running further than sight

quotes.text: the closest thing I could compare it to would be like a Greek or a Roman temple, but it was pearlescent white.
an enormous gorgeous pearlescent glowing white building that looked like it was a Greek or Roman Temple
off to my right, all the way down as far as I could see, were these beautiful white marble columns.
it had the huge white columns in front and a and a huge number of stairs, just so many stairs
vibrantly white with many steps leading up to it and huge columns in front.

places.notes: The most strongly cv-enriched item in this region: 0.71% overall but 3.31% at cv>=23, a 4.7x enrichment. Part of that is one experiencer (Karen Thomas) retelling the same NDE in several interviews, all of which score high, so the enrichment is inflated; but independent accounts (pjxqvZQNFWY / u-_bkoxO0uM, uGMtd3YN3B0, g2QgPL2Q06w) describe the same columned white hall with steps.

places.name: The Library / Hall of Records
places.description: A building whose interior is shelves, scrolls and books rising past the limit of sight, with long tables where spirits sit and study. Reading is not reading: you think of what you want to know and it downloads. Some are told this hall holds the Book of Life; others call it the Akashic Records and say every event past and future is stored there. A recurring detail is that the ceiling cannot be found - the shelves just keep going up.

aliases.note: the plainest and most common word
often described as a building, not an abstraction: 'a big building up in heaven'
sometimes a single enormous book on a stand or table rather than a room
one speaker coins it herself and says she isn't sure that's its real name
one speaker's own name for the same thing, described as a crystallized theatre
with long corridors of books and scrolls radiating out

And I called it the Hall of Knowledge, but I'm not sure if that's what it was really called.

places.notes: Precision is only fair (0.62). The word 'akashic' pulls in a lot of post-NDE spiritual practice ('I became an Akashic record reader') rather than in-experience description, and 'book of life' is sometimes purely scriptural citation. The in-experience core - a building full of books and scrolls entered with a guide - is smaller than the 5.57% headline but is present in some of the highest-cvNDE documents in the corpus.

places.name: The Halls of Learning
places.description: A building or complex of buildings understood, without being told, to be a university or school. Souls go there between lives to study anything - other planets, other galaxies, the mechanics of a coming lifetime. Some see actual classrooms with chairs and desks and a teacher explaining. One speaker was told he could not go in yet. Another describes rooms that open an aperture in the wall as you approach and close behind you.

aliases.note: usually plural, and usually listed alongside halls of knowledge, healing and music
'almost like, just like school'
the phrase people use when they have no name for it

places.notes: Main precision loss is the near-universal metaphor 'Earth is a school / a classroom', which is a doctrine drawn FROM the experience rather than a place inside it; the negative_regex targets it. The literal halls (a building you can approach, enter, be refused entry to) are a smaller but robust subset. Mildly enriched with cvNDE (3.38% -> 4.42%).

places.name: The Temple / Cathedral
places.description: A place of worship in the otherworld, distinct from the library and the school. Descriptions cluster into two shapes: a cathedral with spires going up thousands of feet, pews and a long central corridor scaled far beyond human size; and a crystal temple of light that radiates more brightly than the sun and appears as you approach. A third variant, the healing temple, is where the imprints and traumas carried in the soul are dissolved.

aliases.note: used even by non-religious speakers as a size-and-shape comparison
overlaps with the healing place; the same structure named devotionally
used by one speaker to say she got only as far as heaven's entryway

places.regex: healing temple|temple of (light|healing|knowledge|wisdom|god)|(a|the|this|huge|magnificent|enormous|beautiful|great) cathedral|cathedral[- ]like|(a|the) chapel\b|church (in heaven|there)|(temple|sanctuary) (there|in heaven|of light)
places.negative_regex: your body is a temple|you are the temple of god|right temple|left temple|his temple|hit my temple|sphinx temple|vedanta temple|buddhist temple|cathedral high school|national cathedral|durham cathedral

quotes.text: I find myself at the doorway of a magnificent cathedral. We're talking spires that go up thousands of feet.
A crystal temple of light that shone more radiant than the sun began to appear before me.
I went to this city, there's a crystalline city, and I went into this cathedral
I would call it like into the Healing Temple.

places.notes: Weakest precision in this region (~0.5): 'temple' is heavily polluted by the anatomical temple, earthly Buddhist and Hindu temples visited in biography, and the Pauline 'your body is a temple'. Also the only structure here that is LESS common among the best-evidenced accounts (3.32% at cv>=13 falling to 2.21% at cv>=23), which is worth flagging - explicitly religious architecture may be more expectation-shaped than the generic columned hall.

places.name: The Throne Room
places.description: A chamber containing a seat of authority. Reports split sharply: a minority describe arriving at a real room - steps up to a platform, a huge throne, sometimes two identical white thrones cut from marble, translucent carved artwork like emeralds and diamonds set into the tiles - while a large number invoke the throne only to deny it ('it was not an old man with a beard on a throne judging me'). Both usages are counted here because both are the corpus reasoning about the same structure.

aliases.term: a big chair like a king
aliases.note: a small child's wording, corrected to 'throne' by the adult interviewer
cut from pure white marble, square and angular

places.regex: throne room|throne of god|(saw|there was|sitting on|seated on|sat on|upon) (a|the|this|his|huge|big|great|golden|white) throne
places.negative_regex: not an old man|old man with a long white beard|beard sitting on a throne|game of thrones
sensory: three steps up to a platform, throne on the third step
thrones square and angular, cut from pure white marble

There I saw three steps and on the third step I saw there was a huge throne
I looked up and I saw two men sitting on big white thrones.

places.notes: Roughly half the matches are the negation formula ('God was NOT an old man on a throne'), which is itself one of the most stereotyped sentences in the whole corpus. Slightly LESS common among the best-evidenced accounts. Use negative_regex to isolate the affirmative subset.

places.name: The Garden
places.description: A cultivated, tended place rather than wild landscape: flowers in beds, pavers and paving stones, arbours, a stone archway to enter through, sometimes a fence or gate around it. It is very often the first thing seen on arrival, and it is where deceased relatives are waiting. What makes it a place rather than scenery is that the plants are conscious - flowers greet the visitor by name, a sunflower speaks, the grass is aware of being walked on.

aliases.note: by far the most common phrasing
spoken as a known destination: 'everybody talks about the garden'
picket fence, rose arbour, golden light from the windows of the house behind
used as comparison, sometimes as the place one is expelled FROM on return
used by congenitally blind experiencers who stress it was 'a place full of light'

Precision loss is mostly earthly gardening biography and speakers listing the garden as an expectation they did NOT get.

places.name: The Gate
places.description: The entrance structure to the city or to heaven, and the point at which the question of whether you may enter is decided. Some see many gates of which only one is open; some see a narrow gate beside a wide one; some are set down just inside it. A recurring reinterpretation: the gate is not a barrier keeping people out but an energetic threshold that cleanses whoever passes through. A large minority mention gates specifically to say they expected them and did not find any.

aliases.note: far more often invoked as an expectation than as something seen
Revelation-framed; eleven closed, one open
explicitly not a fence - a cleansing threshold
used when the shape has no hinges or bars

places.notes: The gate is the most culturally pre-loaded structure in the region, and its frequency DROPS at the highest cvNDE stratum (5.25% at cv>=13 down to 3.31% at cv>=23) - the opposite of the city and the columned hall. That is a meaningful negative signal worth preserving.

places.name: The Door
places.description: A single door, usually oversized, standing where a decision has to be made. It is white, or golden, or glass, or three metres tall, and it is explained to the visitor that passing through it is irreversible. Sometimes there is not one door but thousands - golden doors receding down a corridor without end, each opening onto something different. A few insist it was an entirely ordinary wooden door with light coming through, and that the ordinariness is the point.

aliases.note: 'those doors must have been about 3m tall'
in front of the golden city
down a corridor that never ends

aliases.term: a massive door made out of glass
aliases.note: with glass hinge pins that could not work on earth

places.name: The Portal / Archway
places.description: An opening that is not a door and not a tunnel: an aperture that appears in the air, spins open, or simply is, and through which another world is directly visible. People reach for 'portal' when the thing has no frame, no hinges and no length. Some see a forest or a green field through it as though through a window; others go through it and arrive somewhere instantly. The archway variant has a definite arch shape and colours the speaker cannot name.

aliases.note: the corpus's own preferred word for a frameless opening
'a huge doorway without a door, because it's just this huge archway'
one speaker's name for a simple, unornamented arch that opened to show the meaning of life

aliases.term: a slowly spinning white light, up and open like a portal

Speakers are unusually explicit that a portal is NOT a tunnel ('it wasn't a tunnel per se but it was like a portal of energy'), which makes this a genuinely separate structure from the tunnel region rather than a synonym. Precision loss is overwhelmingly the modern web sense of 'portal'.

places.name: The Staircase
places.description: Steps that must be climbed. Two distinct forms: a brilliant white staircase rising out of the ground into the sky with no visible top, which the dying person crawls toward hoping to be found; and a long flight of stone steps leading up to the entrance of a great building, worn hollow in the centre by everyone who has walked them before. The second form is often accompanied by other spirits going up and coming down.

aliases.note: going up as far as the eye can see, into the clouds
several speakers use the phrase self-consciously, calling it 'the proverbial'
ancient, mossy, cold, slippery, worn down in the middle
with huge steps, no visible end
the approach to the columned hall

Some of that comes from the same high-scoring narrators who describe the columned hall (the stairs are its approach), so the two should be treated as partially the same finding.

places.name: The Nursery
places.description: A building, or an area with a large green space around it, where infants are. Speakers are told - usually because they ask what that beautiful building is - that this is where babies who died before or at birth, including the unborn, are raised and taught until they understand. There are attendants: angels, family members, people specifically trained for it. Children are seen running, playing and growing there, and some describe wanting to come back after death to work in it.

aliases.note: the word given to the experiencer by a guide, not chosen by them

aliases.term: an area where the babies and the unborn fetuses are brought
a place where souls were born and nurtured and grown
aliases.note: pre-birth framing rather than post-death
one speaker's term for Earth itself, by analogy

places.negative_regex: nursery rhyme|nursery rhyming|flower nursery|nursery school|hospital nursery|worked in a nursery|to nursery in the morning|children's nursery song

I did see a place where babies go, and they're attended to by, um, angels
I remember what I like to describe as a nursery. And it seemed to be a place where souls were born and or nurtured and grown.

places.notes: Doubles in prevalence between the whole corpus and the cv>=18 stratum (1.23% -> 2.35%). Remaining precision loss after the lookarounds is hospital nurseries recalled from infancy and earthly childcare biography. Note the split between the post-death nursery (children who died) and the pre-birth nursery (souls not yet incarnated) - same building, opposite direction of travel.

places.name: The Healing Place
places.description: A building or chamber where souls are repaired. Descriptions include pools of living water that people are lowered into, a curved room with a defined curvature that guides call a healing chamber, and 'a spiritual hospital' where those who died traumatically or by suicide are brought gently to awareness of what has happened. The work done there is described as being at the atomic or energetic level - stitching, repairing, flushing damage out with light.

aliases.note: filled with living water - 'the water was alive'
curved, no physical representation, but a defined curvature

places.name: The Mansion / My Father's House
places.description: A dwelling: a house, a mansion, a home that is recognisably yours. Some are shown a specific house on a bluff or a cottage with a rose arbour and told, or decide, that it is theirs. Others enter a white mansion whose corridor holds thousands of golden doors, each room a different world. The Johannine 'in my Father's house are many rooms' is quoted constantly, but usually to explain something the speaker saw, not to substitute for it - the rooms are read as levels or realms, not bedrooms.

aliases.note: quoted from John 14:2, glossed as many levels or many worlds

aliases.term: in my Father's house are many rooms

aliases.note: described as entry points to more of the beyond, thresholds that are alive
'there were houses, but we don't need houses because we don't sleep'
recognition of a dwelling as one's own
golden light streaming from the windows at dusk; God is inside

places.notes: Only one hit at cv>=23, so the apparent collapse in the top stratum is not reliable. A recurring rhetorical move worth noting: several speakers are shown a mansion specifically so that a guide can ask 'can you contain God in that mansion?' and then dissolve it into trees, clouds and earths - the building exists to be outgrown.

places.name: The Room
places.description: A bounded interior with no discernible architecture: you know you are in a room because there is an inside, but the walls may be cloud, atmosphere, or nothing at all. Most often white or brilliantly bright; sometimes round, with aisles radiating from all sides and open sky and stars overhead. It has no reference points, so people cannot say whether it is small or vast. This is frequently where a being of light appears, or where a life review is presented.

aliases.note: the commonest form; often the whole of what was seen

aliases.term: a room without walls - the walls were made out of the atmosphere

aliases.note: aisles from all sides; sky and stars visible above

places.notes: Rises steadily with cvNDE (3.29% -> 5.52%). The 'white room' is the minimal built structure in the corpus - the least furnished thing that still counts as being somewhere rather than nowhere, and it sits right at the boundary with the void/darkness region.

places.name: The Golden Road / Streets of Gold
places.description: The paved surfaces of the built world: streets of gold, golden roads, cobbled roads with guttering, a path of light laid across water toward the sun. Some walk on gold and say everything underfoot was gold; one describes cobbled pathways followed for what she estimates as thousands of kilometres, through valleys and past lakes, into a city. A large share of mentions are people naming 'streets of gold' as the cliche they expected and did not receive.

aliases.note: the single most quoted expectation about heaven in the corpus
'crystal cities and golden roads with diamonds reflecting the universe'

places.notes: Precision ~0.5 and the number falls at the top stratum (one hit at cv>=23). Roughly half of all 'streets of gold' mentions in the corpus are explicit denials: 'I saw nothing like that', 'no streets paved with gold', 'no gold streets, nothing like that'. That negative pattern is itself the finding - the golden street is the corpus's canonical example of an expectation the experience does not honour.

places.name: The Wall / Fence / Barrier
places.description: A built or quasi-built limit that cannot be crossed. It appears as a white fence in the distance across a meadow, a low wooden fence approached step by step, a picket fence, or - most often - an invisible barrier with no material at all which nevertheless stops both the visitor and the dead who are waiting on the other side. Everyone understands the same rule without being told: cross it and there is no return.

aliases.note: the commonest form; nobody can come through it in either direction
seen at a distance across a meadow, with low shrubbery beyond
understood afterwards as the symbol of passing over for good
something is behind it, and you cannot go behind it

places.notes: Deliberately narrow regex - the unconstrained forms of 'wall' and 'fence' match 25% of the corpus and are almost entirely earthly. At this tightness it is genuinely rare (0.53%) but doubles by cv>=23. Overlaps the border/boundary region; included here only for the constructed forms (fence, wall, gate-as-limit), not the river or line-of-light forms.

places.name: The Bridge
places.description: A crossing over water. Small, often stone or wooden, sometimes described as ornamental rather than structural - 'like a garden ornament'. What happens on it matters more than what it is made of: people are seen walking across, and the moment they reach the far side they stop walking and simply float away. Several experiencers get to the point where the bridge begins and are turned back there, making it the exact place where the decision to return is taken.

aliases.term: a stone bridge over a rippling brook
the point where the bridge starts
aliases.note: the return decision point

places.notes: Flat across strata. Precision losses are the medical 'bridge' device, the metaphorical bridge between beliefs, and the bridge of the nose. Distinct from the wall/fence barrier: the bridge is a boundary you are permitted to approach and even step onto, which is why it shows up in return-decision narratives rather than in 'I was stopped' narratives.
